subject: NovarEst qualification sync — clarify throughput, streaming, and benchmark plan
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@novarest.com>, Tom Patel <tom.patel@novarest.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + proposed benchmark plan and asks

Hi Elena / Tom — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we schedule a formal run.

Call highlights (what I heard):
- Primary goal: qualify Redwood for production inference on NovarEst’s personalization pipeline (real-time scoring + streaming response to UI).
- Targets you mentioned: p95 latency goal for non-streamed responses ~ < 150 ms, p99 < 300 ms; streaming first-byte window <= 300 ms; concurrency in steady state ~ 150 active sessions; burst to 400 concurrent sessions for short windows.
- Throughput: peak token throughput estimate ~ 40k tokens/minute during nightly jobs; interactive path ~ 6k tokens/minute.
- Key constraints: must validate in us-west region, and final acceptance run needs to be within your VPC / on-prem environment for security review (we discussed an initial hosted run for quick feedback).

What we propose for the qualification benchmark (attached materials):
1) Measurement spec (attached streaming-slo-spec.xlsx) — explicit metric definitions (latency buckets, p50/p95/p99, first-byte latency for streaming), sampling periods, and required reproducibility steps.
2) Prompt set (attached novarest-benchmark-prompt-set-v1.json) — canonical prompts for the interactive and batch paths; please review and confirm whether to substitute with your canonical inputs.
3) Harness & repro steps (attached benchmark-harness-instructions.md) — how we drive load, environment variables, and required artifacts for deterministic runs.

Asks from your side before we schedule the run:
- Confirm the SLO thresholds above or provide updated targets in the spreadsheet.
- Confirm whether we should use the attached prompt set as-is or replace with your sample corpus (and provide a small sanitized sample if replacing).
- Confirm preferred environment for the initial run: Redwood hosted (fastest) or your VPC (preferred for final acceptance).
- Indicate any additional observability hooks you require (tracing headers, request ids) — we can instrument the harness to send them.

Proposed next steps / owners:
- Elena: confirm SLO targets and whether to use our prompt set (reply by EOD Wed).
- Lauren: will propose two candidate windows for an initial hosted run once Elena confirms prompts/environment.
- Neha: will own measurement spec validation and reproducibility checklist.

If that all looks good I’ll ask Lauren to pick windows and we’ll queue a quick smoke run to validate the harness.

Thanks — Markus

--
Markus Klein
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai

From: Elena Rossi <elena@novarest.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Patel <tom.patel@novarest.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 17:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + proposed benchmark plan and asks

Thanks Markus — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers inline below and a couple clarifying Qs: 

- SLOs: The p95/p99 bands you listed are close; we need the final acceptance bar at p99 < 250 ms for non-streamed (our product latency budget is tight). For streaming first-byte we need <= 250 ms ideally; 300 ms acceptable for now but include the 250 ms as aspirational. I’ve updated the streaming-slo-spec.xlsx with notes.

- Prompt set: we prefer to use a small sanitized subset of our production prompts for the interactive path (we’ll send a 100-record sample today). For the batch path you can use your provided set.

- Environment: initial hosted run is fine for iteration. Final acceptance will need to run inside our VPC (we’ll provide a short VPN jump host or temporary peering). We expect to validate the final run with our security team present; can Redwood provide an HLD for the final run?

- Observability: please include request-id propagation and a header we can map to our tracing (x-novarest-trace-id). Also capture token-level timing and first-byte timestamps.

We’re OK to proceed with an initial hosted run next week after we share the sample prompts. I’ve attached a short doc (redlines) with our notes on the measurement spreadsheet.

FWIW we also want to ensure the harness can reproduce streaming behavior (partial chunk sizes and timings) — we will include examples in the prompt sample.

Thanks — Elena

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + proposed benchmark plan and asks

Elena — great, thanks for the quick turn. We can meet the 250 ms p99 aspiration in many configurations; Neha will draft a measurement plan that separates model-only latency from end-to-end platform latency so we can identify optimization levers.

Hosting notes: initial hosted run will let us iterate fast. For the VPC acceptance run we will provide an architecture overview (HLD) and a checklist for the peering step.

I’ll ask Lauren to schedule candidate windows; Lauren — can you propose two 90-minute slots next week (Wed/Thu preferred) and include the smoke run + one full-run slot?

Markus

Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Scheduling + measurement owners and reproducibility checklist

Hi team — following Markus’ ask, proposed schedule and concrete run plan below. I’ve attached the harness instructions and a reproducibility checklist to this message.

Proposed windows (90 minute blocks) for initial hosted runs (pick one):
- Option A: Wed 2026-08-05 09:00–10:30 PT (smoke run + quick full pass)
- Option B: Thu 2026-08-06 13:00–14:30 PT (smoke run + full pass)

Measurement owners & responsibilities:
- Neha Kapoor: measurement spec validation, dataset / prompt handling, result validation.
- Rishi Malhotra: harness orchestration, load shaping and streaming chunk simulator.
- Markus Klein: experiment sign-off and final acceptance criteria.

Reproducibility checklist (high level):
- Anchored prompt set (sha256 hash in harness instructions).
- Seeded randomness flags and stable model revision pinning.
- Full request/response logs for at least one run (sanitized) + token-level timing.
- Run artifacts: console trace, raw harness metrics (CSV), aggregated latency histograms, and a short summary report.

Next actions / owners:
- Elena: send the 100-record sanitized prompt sample by EOD today (we’ll ingest and place in the shared Drive).
- NovarEst sec: indicate preferred VPC peering approach (VPN jump host vs temporary peering).
- Lauren: I’ll create the Drive folder and a HubSpot activity; link below.

Links / artifacts:
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bBenchmarkDriveLink
- HubSpot: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deals/NE-2026-73

Attachments: benchmark-harness-instructions.md, streaming-slo-spec.xlsx, novarest-benchmark-prompt-set-v1.json

Thanks — Lauren
